Constipation: Uncomfortable bodily effect: infrequent or hard bowel movements · opposite of Diarrhea

Frequent urination: Uncomfortable bodily effect: needing to urinate more often than usual · opposite of Difficulty urinating

Language suppression: Cognitive suppression: reduced ability to use and understand speech · not Glossolalia
Laughter fits: Physical alteration: uncontrollable spontaneous laughter with nothing funny behind it · not Increased sense of humor
Machinescapes: Hallucinatory state: vast, intricate hallucinated mechanical landscapes felt as well as seen, typical of salvia · not Geometry

Runny nose: Uncomfortable bodily effect: the nose fills with mucus · not Increased phlegm production, which is the throat

Settings, sceneries, and landscapes: Hallucinatory state: the environments a hallucination takes place in · not Scenarios and plots, which are the events
Shadow people: Hallucinatory state: patches of shadow seen as living beings, often in peripheral vision · a subtype of Autonomous entity
Shakiness: Uncomfortable bodily effect: trembling of the hands, limbs or body · not Muscle twitching, which is localized
Skin flushing: Uncomfortable bodily effect: sudden reddening of the skin with rushing warmth · not Increased perspiration

Spatial disorientation: Physical alteration: losing track of one's own position or motion in space · not Dizziness, which is spinning
Spirituality enhancement: Transpersonal state: a shift in beliefs about existence, other people and what is meaningful · not Unity and interconnectedness

Gustatory: Sensory heading for taste effects · sibling of Olfactory; together they form Smell & Taste
Gustatory Effects: Effect subcategory under Smell & Taste Effects for everything that alters taste · not Olfactory Effects
Hallucinatory States: Visual effect subcategory: wholly new dreamlike content added to perception, same grouping as Hallucinatory Effects · not Novel States or Distortions
Impairment: Cognitive effect subcategory: thinking, memory and judgement reduced · not Coordination, which is physical; not Suppressions
Multisensory: Sensory heading for effects across several senses, short form of Multisensory Effects · not Visual or Auditory alone
Neurological: Physical effect subcategory for brain-related discomforts, short form of Neurological Effects · not Cardiovascular
Novel States: Cognitive effect subcategory for states unlike ordinary consciousness, short form of Novel Cognitive States · not Hallucinatory States or Psychological States
Olfactory: Sensory heading for smell effects · sibling of Gustatory; together they form Smell & Taste
Olfactory Effects: Effect subcategory under Smell & Taste Effects for everything that alters smell · not Gustatory Effects
Perception: Cognitive effect subcategory: how the world, time and self are perceived · not Analytical or Emotional
Relaxation: Physical effect subcategory: calming, muscle-loosening effects · not Sedation or Sleep
Respiratory: Physical effect subcategory: breathing effects · not Cardiovascular
Sleep: Physical effect subcategory: sleep and dream effects · not Sedation or Relaxation
Smell & Taste: Sensory heading grouping Olfactory and Gustatory, short form of Smell & Taste Effects · keep the ampersand style
Social: Cognitive effect subcategory: sociability, empathy and communication · not Emotional
Suppressions: Effect subcategory heading: a facet is decreased, under Visual, Cognitive and Physical alike · not Amplifications or Enhancements
Tactile: Sensory heading for touch effects, short form of Tactile Effects · sibling of Visual and Auditory
Temperature: Physical effect subcategory: body heat and its regulation · not Autonomic
Transpersonal: Cognitive effect subcategory for one's place in the universe and reality, short form of Transpersonal States · not Perception
Uncomfortable: Physical effect subcategory heading for unpleasant bodily effects · opposite of Comfortable
Visual: Sensory heading for sight effects, short form of Visual Effects · sibling of Auditory and Tactile
Rare: Frequency 1 of 5 on the effect intensity scales: seldom reported · below Uncommon
Uncommon: Frequency 2 of 5 on the effect intensity scales: reported by a minority · between Rare and Common
Common: Frequency 3 of 5 on the effect intensity scales: reported by many · a scale position, not ordinary
Frequent: Frequency 4 of 5 on the effect intensity scales: reported by most · between Common and Near universal
Near universal: Frequency 5 of 5 on the effect intensity scales: reported by almost everyone · above Frequent
